D-ADJ: 'adjacent cells, whose turn resolves first' is undecided; player-then-hazard, with the winning ply ending the run BEFORE hazard motion, is what makes level 05 a WIN and not a death
D-BLOCK: moving into the cell a hazard stands on is undecided; blocked makes a hazard a living wall, which is the ONLY mechanism in this contract that destroys the player's route -- see 4F1
D-BLOCKED-TURN: a legal letter aimed at rock is CONSUMED: `moves` does not advance, the turn count does, and a hazard already on a road steps closer. The rejected reading -- 'only a successful move is a turn' -- makes waiting safe by walking into a wall, which is the same rule as [D-STOP] wearing a costume; the two are decided together and reported separately because `blocked` and `waited` are different counters and the record must be able to tell which one a run filled
D-BOUNDS: B2: bounds are checked in the transition function; walking off the board is impossible, and an unbounded walk is an error only in the sense that it never happens
D-CLOCK: the paragraph says a hazard 'can arrive' through tunnels and never says when it moves; per-player-turn is the only reading that makes the run a pure function of the answer stream
D-END: does a run that collects the last pearl on the ply a hazard would step onto it count?  Decided YES.  Level 05 exists to exercise exactly this clause
D-HAZCOLL: two hazards in one cell is not expressible in the prose and is decided: they block each other, which makes a junction into a thing a plan can use
D-NEIGHBOUR: the boundary is one rule, so it is ONE function: `neighbour(state, cell, delta)` applies wrap and nothing else decides where a coordinate is.  It is recorded as a decision because it was found as a bug: a copy of these two lines in `reachable_cells()` reduced the coordinate AFTER adding it to `seen`, so on any `wrap=True` reading the mobility flood fill expanded off the edge forever and the process died.  The frozen reading cannot reach it (wrap is off), which is why it survived review -- and why [B2]'s rule is not only 'check the bounds in the transition function' but 'there is one place that knows the bounds'
D-OBJ: 'solved' is not defined by the paragraph; collecting every target is the only reading that uses the sentence it does provide ('a target is collected by moving into its cell')
D-STOP: the paragraph never says the player may stop; WAIT is in the ALPHABET anyway, because R3 puts the answer shape in the grammar and a game that permits a pause the grammar forbids makes a correct answer a failure
D-T0: the paragraph says a hazard cannot reach the player except through tunnels, so its route does NOT exist through UNDIGGED soil. Measured scope, stated here because the first draft of this sentence said 'at time zero nothing moves' and level 04 refutes it: `_` is ground the level AUTHOR dug, so 04 has a hazard armed at distance 2 before the entrant has typed anything. A new level cannot arm a hazard; an authored tunnel run can -- which is the difference between this clause and [D-TIEBREAK]'s determinism, and why the item set contains one of each
D-TARGET: 'collected' has no stated consequence; removal is the reading under which the word means something
D-TIEBREAK: the paragraph permits more than one hazard and never says what two hazards wanting the same cell do. Frozen to reading order because the EXHAUSTIVE PROOF depends on it: a randomised tie-break makes the state key incomplete and every number in this cabinet unreplayable. The choice costs nothing on any of the five levels (measured: 4F item 6) and buys determinism with no seed -- which is why it is in the contract and not in a comment
D-WRAP: the grid is bounded, it does not wrap; 'a grid of soil' with no torus language is a bounded grid, and wrapping would make the enclosure measurement meaningless

R_digdug_levels.denominator_rule: NEVER_STARTED sits OUTSIDE both denominators and is counted separately (B1); an item where every answer was unreadable is still EMITTED and is still in the denominator, which is what makes the zero rule bite.

R_digdug_levels.loose_give_up_note: answers that LOOKED like an abstention to a substring test but were scored not_an_action by the frozen exact-token list. DIAGNOSTIC ONLY -- never scored, never folded into give_up [R1].

wait.note: WAIT is in the ALPHABET because the prose does not settle whether the player may stop, and R3 puts the answer shape in the grammar [D-STOP].

grammar.wasd: not_an_action (NOT synonyms).  D is DOWN, never RIGHT [D-WASD] -- a synonym table would change the GAME without changing any counter.
grammar.truncation: NEVER.  multi-char -> not_an_action.  GIVE UP is not G.
grammar.give_up_match: EXACT on casefold + whitespace-collapsed line; punctuation NOT stripped [D-TOKENS]
grammar.give_up_diagnostic: loose_give_up is a substring test, RECORDED ONLY, never scored, never folded into give_up [R1]
grammar.rule_precedence: A1 line count, A2 give_up, A3 alphabet, A4 near-miss, A5 multi-char  [D-ORDER]
grammar.line_rule: answer is the single non-empty line; 2+ non-empty lines -> not_an_action (multi_line), never one of them
grammar.whitespace_rule: the chosen line is stripped; ' U ' reads as U

exit_code_table.1: INSTRUMENT NOT PROVEN -- self-test / instrument-check / level verification failed
exit_code_table.2: ZERO MEASURED -- ERROR, never a verdict
exit_code_table.3: USAGE -- unknown entrant or bad arguments
exit_code_table.4: ENTRANT NEVER STARTED -- counted separately from played-and-failed
exit_code_table.5: RECORD NOT WRITTEN -- a run with no record is not a run
exit_code_table.6: CONTRACT NOT FROZEN (or it drifted) -- no entrant plays
